q.s: The famous steatite bust of the bearded 'Priest-King' of the Indus Valley Civilisation was found at:
q.x: The Priest-King, a steatite bust of a bearded man in a trefoil-patterned shawl, comes from Mohenjodaro.

q.s: The red sandstone male torso, a notable piece of Harappan stone sculpture, was found at:
q.x: The red sandstone male torso is from Harappa; the steatite Priest-King is from Mohenjodaro.

q.s: The Lotus Sutra (Saddharma Pundarika), composed in Sanskrit, is a sacred text of:
q.x: The Lotus Sutra and the Prajnaparamita texts belong to Mahayana; the Pali canon is the Hinayana (Theravada) scripture.

q.s: The Kangyur and the Tengyur together form the scriptural canon of:
q.x: Kangyur (the Buddha's word) and Tengyur (commentaries) make up the Tibetan Buddhist canon.

q.s: The Barabar caves near Gaya, among the earliest rock-cut caves of India, were gifted to the Ajivikas by:
q.x: Ashoka gifted the Barabar caves to the Ajivikas; his grandson Dasharatha gifted the Nagarjuni caves.

q.s: Which Ashokan edict names the Ajivikas along with the Brahmanas, the Sangha and the Nirgranthas?
q.x: The Seventh Pillar Edict lists the Ajivikas among the sects the Dhamma Mahamatras looked after; the Thirteenth Rock Edict is about the Kalinga War.

q.s: The killing and deportation of lakhs of people in the Kalinga War, which filled Ashoka with remorse, are recorded in his:
q.x: Rock Edict XIII records about one lakh killed and one and a half lakh deported in Kalinga.

q.s: After the Kalinga War, Ashoka gave up wars of conquest and adopted the policy of:
q.x: Remorse over Kalinga led Ashoka to replace conquest by war (Bherighosha) with conquest by Dhamma (Dhammavijaya).

q.s: Which site in Andhra Pradesh carries both the fourteen Major Rock Edicts and a Minor Rock Edict of Ashoka?
q.x: Erragudi (Kurnool district) has the 14 Major Rock Edicts and a Minor Rock Edict; Rajula Mandagiri has only a Minor Rock Edict.

q.s: The Ashokan edicts found at Erragudi and Rajula Mandagiri in Andhra Pradesh are written in the Prakrit language and the:
q.x: The Andhra edicts are in Prakrit and Brahmi; Kharosthi was used in the north-west.

q.s: The official (court) language of the Delhi Sultanate was:
q.x: Persian was the language of administration; Arabic was the language of religion and theology.

q.s: The form of Hindavi/Urdu that developed in the Deccan is known as:
q.x: Dakhni (Deccani) Urdu developed under the Bahmani and the Deccan Sultanates.

q.s: Who succeeded Aurangzeb on the Mughal throne in 1707?
q.x: Bahadur Shah I ruled 1707-1712; Jahandar Shah followed (1712-13), then Farrukhsiyar (1713-19).

q.s: Which Later Mughal is NOT correctly matched with his reign?
q.x: Ahmad Shah ruled 1748-1754 and was succeeded by Alamgir II.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of Sikh Guru and contribution is NOT correctly matched?
o: Angad Dev – Standardised the Gurmukhi script
Tegh Bahadur – Founded Anandpur Sahib (Chak Nanki)
q.x: The 22 Manjis were organised by Amar Das; Arjan Dev compiled the Adi Granth (1604).

q.s: The Adi Granth was compiled in 1604 by:
q.x: Guru Arjan Dev compiled the Adi Granth and installed it at the Harmandir Sahib in 1604.

q.s: The Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh, which is critical of Akbar's religious policy, was written by:
q.x: Badauni wrote the Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh; Abul Fazl, Akbar's court historian, wrote the Akbarnama and the Ain-i-Akbari.

q.s: Abul Fazl, the court historian of Akbar, was the author of the:
q.x: Abul Fazl wrote the Akbarnama, whose third part is the Ain-i-Akbari; the Tabaqat-i-Akbari is by Nizamuddin Ahmad.

q.s: The Tiruvaymoli, one of the most revered Vaishnava hymn collections in Tamil, was composed by:
q.x: Nammalvar, the foremost of the Alvars, composed the Tiruvaymoli; Manikkavachakar wrote the Tiruvasagam.

q.s: Who among the following is NOT one of the three Nayanars whose hymns form the Tevaram?
q.x: The Tevaram is the hymns of Appar, Sambandar and Sundarar; Manikkavachakar wrote the Tiruvasagam.

q.s: After the Revolt of 1857, the British mixed the regiments of the Indian army by caste, community and region under a policy known as:
q.x: Mixing regiments let groups balance each other so that they could not combine again as in 1857.

q.s: The farman of Farrukhsiyar granting trade privileges in Bengal to the English East India Company was issued in:
q.x: The 1717 farman (the 'Magna Carta' of the Company) gave it duty-free trade in Bengal.

q.s: The Treaty of Salbai (1782) brought to an end the:
q.x: Salbai (1782) ended the First Anglo-Maratha War; the Treaty of Madras (1769) ended the First Anglo-Mysore War with Haidar Ali.

q.s: Plague Commissioner W.C. Rand was shot dead at Poona in 1897 by:
q.x: The Chapekar brothers shot Rand over the harsh plague measures in Poona.

q.s: In 1879 Vasudev Balwant Phadke organised an armed revolt against the British with the help of the:
q.x: Phadke raised a force of Ramosi peasants in Maharashtra in 1879.

q.s: During the Quit India Movement, the British lifted the ban on the Communist Party of India in July 1942 because the party had:
o: merged with the Congress Socialist Party
decided to support the war effort
q.x: The CPI called the war a 'People's War' after the German attack on the USSR and backed the war effort, so the ban was lifted on 23 July 1942.

q.s: In Andhra, Tenneti Viswanatham led the Salt Satyagraha of 1930 at:
q.x: Tenneti Viswanatham led it at Visakhapatnam and Bhimili; Dandu Narayana Raju at Mattapalem.

q.s: Who led the Salt Satyagraha at Mypadu in Nellore district in April 1930?
q.x: Bezawada Gopala Reddy made salt at Mypadu on 11 April 1930; Ravi Narayana Reddy led it at Ramachandrapuram.

q.s: Operation Polo, the police action that integrated Hyderabad State with the Indian Union, was carried out in:
q.x: Indian troops entered Hyderabad on 13 September 1948 and the Nizam announced a ceasefire on 17 September.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Operation Polo is correct?
o: K.M. Munshi led the Indian troops into Hyderabad.
The Nizam announced a ceasefire on 13 September 1948.
The operation followed the Nizam's signing of the Instrument of Accession.
J.N. Chaudhuri became the Military Governor of Hyderabad after the operation.
q.x: Major General J.N. Chaudhuri became Military Governor; K.M. Munshi was India's Agent-General; the Nizam had only signed a Standstill Agreement, which he breached.

q.s: Which of the following Hindu Code laws was NOT enacted in 1956?
q.x: The Hindu Marriage Act came in 1955; the other three were enacted in 1956.

q.s: Which Article of the Constitution gives minorities the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice?
q.x: Article 30 protects minority educational institutions; Article 29 protects the language, script and culture of any section of citizens.

q.s: The Borra Caves in the Ananthagiri hills of Visakhapatnam district were discovered in 1807 by:
q.x: William King discovered the Borra Caves in 1807; Robert Bruce Foote is known for prehistoric finds in South India.

q.s: The Ketavaram Mesolithic rock paintings of Andhra Pradesh are located in which district?
q.x: Ketavaram rock paintings are in Kurnool district.

q.s: The Brihatkatha of Gunadhya, associated with the Satavahana age, was written in:
q.x: By legend Gunadhya gave up Sanskrit after losing a bet with Sarvavarma and wrote the Brihatkatha in Paishachi.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a retelling of Gunadhya's Brihatkatha?
q.x: The Gathasaptashati is Hala's Prakrit anthology; the Kathasaritsagara is by Somadeva of Kashmir and the Brihatkathamanjari by Kshemendra.

q.s: Which of the following Vijayanagara departments is NOT correctly paired with its function?
q.x: Dharmasana was the judicial department; Bhandara was the treasury.

q.s: The Shakti peetha goddess worshipped at Srisailam is:
q.x: Bhramaramba is the Shakti at Srisailam; Manikyamba is at Draksharamam and Jogulamba at Alampur.

q.s: The steps from the Srisailam temple to Patalaganga were completed in 1346 by the Reddi ruler:
q.x: Prolaya Vema Reddy built the Patalaganga steps; Anavema Reddy built the Veera Siromandapam.

q.s: The mukha mandapam of the Mallikarjuna temple at Srisailam is credited to the Vijayanagara ruler:
q.x: Harihara II built the mukha mandapam at Srisailam.

q.s: The bronze statues of Krishnadevaraya with his queens Chinna Devi and Tirumala Devi are found at:
q.x: Krishnadevaraya's bronze statues with his queens stand in the Tirumala temple.

q.s: The Surabhi theatre of Andhra Pradesh grew out of which traditional art form?
q.x: Vanarasa Govinda Rao, from a leather-puppet family, replaced the puppets with live actors in Keechaka Vadham.

q.s: The Surabhi theatre began with the staging of Keechaka Vadham at Sorugu, a village in which present district?
q.x: Sorugu is near Jammalamadugu in Kadapa district.

q.s: The Second Buddhist Council at Vaishali was held under the patronage of:
q.x: The First Council was under Ajatashatru, the Second under Kalashoka, the Third under Ashoka and the Fourth under Kanishka.

q.s: Ashvaghosha and other Mahayana writers of the Kushana age composed their works in:
q.x: Mahayana texts of the Kushana age were in Sanskrit, while early Buddhism used Pali-Prakrit.

q.s: Which of the following does NOT promote social stability in India?
q.x: Regionalism threatens social stability; tolerance, welfare and social justice strengthen it.

q.s: The definition of a minority as a group set apart by race, nationality, religion or language and regarded as different by itself and others was given by:
q.x: This definition is Arnold Rose's; Giddens stressed disadvantage, solidarity and isolation.

q.s: Equal coparcenary rights to daughters by birth were provided by an amendment to the:
q.x: The 2005 amendment to the Hindu Succession Act made daughters coparceners by birth.

q.s: Under the POSH Act, an Internal Complaints Committee must be set up in every workplace with at least:
q.x: Workplaces with 10 or more employees must have an Internal Complaints Committee.

q.s: The Poona Pact between Gandhi and Ambedkar on the representation of the Depressed Classes was signed in:
q.x: The Poona Pact was signed in 1932; Ambedkar's Yeola declaration came in 1935.

q.s: The Karamchedu atrocity against Dalits in Andhra Pradesh took place in:
q.x: Karamchedu was in 1985; the Tsundur massacre was in 1991.

q.s: The Suppression of Immoral Traffic in Women and Girls Act (SITA), 1956 was renamed in 1986 as the:
o: Protection of Women from Exploitation Act
q.x: SITA (1956) became the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act in 1986.

q.s: Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, the offence of trafficking of persons is dealt with in Section:
q.x: Trafficking is in Section 143 of the BNS; Section 370 was the corresponding IPC section.

q.s: Which law of 2013 widened the offence of trafficking to cover slavery, servitude, forced labour and removal of organs?
q.x: The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013, passed after the Verma Committee report, recast the trafficking offence.

q.s: The concept of the 'culture of poverty' was propounded in 1959 by:
q.x: Oscar Lewis introduced the 'culture of poverty'; Nurkse gave the 'vicious circle of poverty'.

q.s: India's official poverty line is based on:
q.x: The poverty line is fixed in terms of monthly per capita consumption expenditure.

q.s: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana, a small-savings scheme for the girl child, was launched in:
q.x: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana came in 2015 under Beti Bachao Beti Padhao; Balika Samriddhi Yojana in 1997.

q.s: The Balika Samriddhi Yojana (1997) is meant for girl children of:
q.x: Balika Samriddhi Yojana covers girls of BPL families.

q.s: Which law was the first in India to recognise aggregators, gig workers and platform workers?
o: Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020
q.x: The Code on Social Security, 2020 first defined gig and platform workers.

q.s: Which State passed the first State law for platform-based gig workers in 2023, with a welfare board funded by a cess on transactions?
q.x: Rajasthan's Platform-Based Gig Workers Act, 2023 was the first such State law.

q.s: Who became the first Governor-General of India under the Charter Act, 1833?
q.x: The 1833 Act made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India, so Bentinck became the first; Warren Hastings was the first Governor-General of Bengal.

q.s: Which of the following features of the Indian Constitution was NOT borrowed from the USSR?
o: Ideals of social, economic and political justice in the Preamble
q.x: The Republic, with liberty, equality and fraternity, is from France; the other three came from the USSR.

q.s: The Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution of India by the:
q.x: The 42nd Amendment added ten duties; the 86th Amendment added the eleventh.

q.s: After the 44th Amendment, the right to property is now a:
q.x: The 44th Amendment (1978) removed property from the Fundamental Rights and placed it in Article 300A.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a Directive Principle of State Policy?
o: Equal justice and free legal aid (Article 39A)
Equal pay for equal work for men and women (Article 39(d))
Free and compulsory education for children aged 6-14 (Article 21A)
q.x: Article 21A, inserted by the 86th Amendment (2002), is a Fundamental Right; the other three are Directive Principles.

q.s: Under the norms of the Right to Education Act, 2009, the pupil-teacher ratio at the primary level is:
q.x: The norm is 30:1 at the primary and 35:1 at the upper-primary level.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT permitted under the Right to Education Act, 2009?
o: Teacher qualifications laid down by the NCTE
A screening test for admission to Class 1
A pupil-teacher ratio of 35:1 at the upper-primary level
Admission of an out-of-school child to an age-appropriate class
q.x: The RTE Act bars any screening procedure and capitation fee for admission.

q.s: The Legislative Assembly of the National Capital Territory of Delhi was provided for by the 69th Amendment under Article:
q.x: Delhi's legislature is under Article 239AA (69th Amendment, 1991); Puducherry's under Article 239A.

q.s: Which of the following Union Territories does NOT have a legislature?
q.x: Lakshadweep has no legislature and comes under the Kerala High Court; the Andaman and Nicobar Islands also have none.

q.s: The President's power to promulgate ordinances when Parliament is not in session is given in Article:
q.x: Article 123 covers the President's ordinances; Article 213 covers the Governor's.

q.s: The ordinance-making power in the Constitution of India was derived from the:
q.x: The ordinance power is a carry-over from the Government of India Act, 1935.

q.s: Under Article 222, the President transfers a judge from one High Court to another after consulting the:
q.x: Transfer of High Court judges is by the President after consulting the CJI; there is no such provision for Supreme Court judges.

q.s: Which of the following taxes is NOT levied by the States?
q.x: Corporation tax is a Union tax; land revenue, agricultural income tax and vehicle taxes are State taxes.

q.s: Under Article 276, the maximum tax a State may levy on professions, trades, callings and employments per person per year is:
q.x: The 60th Amendment (1988) raised the cap from Rs 250 to Rs 2,500 a year.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a recommendation of the Second Administrative Reforms Commission?
o: A code of ethics for civil servants
Lateral entry at the Joint Secretary level
Abolition of right to public services laws
q.x: The Second ARC recommended enacting right to public services laws, not abolishing them.

q.s: The Sarkaria Commission on Centre-State relations was set up by the Central Government in:
q.x: Sarkaria was set up in June 1983 and reported in 1988; Rajamannar (1969) was a Tamil Nadu committee and Punchhi came in 2007.

q.s: Abolition of the All India Services was recommended by the:
q.x: Rajamannar wanted the All India Services abolished; Sarkaria wanted them strengthened.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Supreme Court's judgment in ADR v. Election Commission of India (2024) is correct?
o: It rejected the demand for counting 100% of VVPAT slips.
It ordered a return to paper ballots.
It ordered checks of half the EVMs in every constituency.
It allowed any voter to seek a check of the EVMs.
q.x: The Court rejected 100% VVPAT counting and paper ballots; only second- and third-placed candidates may seek checks.

q.s: Under ADR v. ECI (2024), the second- and third-placed candidates may seek a check of what share of EVMs per constituency?
q.x: They may seek checks of 5% of EVMs per constituency, applying within 7 days of the results.

q.s: Under the Delimitation Act, 2002, the Delimitation Commission is chaired by:
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
q.x: It is chaired by a retired Supreme Court judge; the CEC (or a nominated EC) and the State Election Commissioners are ex officio members.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Delimitation Commission is correct?
o: It redraws constituencies on the basis of the latest census.
It redraws constituencies on the basis of the latest electoral rolls.
It is a constitutional body under Article 324.
It is set up by the Election Commission of India.
q.x: It is set up by the Central Government under an Act of Parliament and works on census figures.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the World Trade Organization is correct?
o: Liberia became its 164th member in July 2016.
Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala is its sixth Director-General.
It came into being on 1 January 1996.
It was created by the Marrakesh Agreement signed in April 1994.
q.x: The WTO began on 1 January 1995; Afghanistan was the 164th member; Okonjo-Iweala is the seventh Director-General.

q.s: Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, the Director-General of the WTO, is from:
q.x: Okonjo-Iweala of Nigeria is the first woman and the first African to head the WTO.

q.s: As per the final figures of Census 2011, India's sex ratio was:
q.x: The final sex ratio was 943 (provisional 940); rural 949 and urban 929.

q.s: As per the final figures of Census 2011, India's child sex ratio (0-6 years) was:
q.x: The final child sex ratio was 918 (provisional 914).

q.s: How many mission cities were covered under the Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM)?
q.x: JNNURM covered 63 mission cities - mainly million-plus cities, State capitals and heritage cities.

q.s: Under JNNURM, small and medium towns were covered by the component called:
q.x: BSUP served the urban poor in mission cities; UIDSSMT covered small and medium towns.

q.s: Under the Smart Cities Mission, the equity of the Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) is shared between the State/UT and the urban local body in the ratio:
q.x: SPV equity is held 50:50 by the State/UT and the ULB.

q.s: Each Smart City's Special Purpose Vehicle is incorporated as a company under the:
o: Municipal Corporations Act of the State
q.x: There is one SPV per city, a limited company under the Companies Act, 2013.

q.s: Organised manufacturing covers registered factories employing 10 or more workers with the aid of power, or how many or more workers without power?
q.x: Under the Factories Act definition: 10+ workers with power, 20+ without.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a component of the inclusive-growth strategy of the Eleventh Five-Year Plan?
q.x: The Eleventh Plan's inclusive growth covered agriculture, employment, poverty reduction and reduction of disparities; capital markets were not part of it.

q.s: The Planning Commission was replaced by NITI Aayog on:
q.x: NITI Aayog came on 1 January 2015; the Plan era ended on 31 March 2017.

q.s: After the 1991 reforms, which of the following helped to cushion India's current account deficit?
o: Growth of IT and outsourcing exports
q.x: Imports grew faster than exports, but IT and outsourcing exports narrowed the current account deficit.

q.s: Under the post-1991 disinvestment policy, ownership and management of a PSU passed to a private buyer who acquired more than:
q.x: Strategic sale gave control to buyers of more than 51%; early disinvestment aimed mainly at raising resources.

q.s: Under the financial-sector reforms after 1991, the role of the RBI was to change from:
o: Banker to the Government to sole lender
q.x: The reforms sought to move the RBI from regulating to facilitating the financial sector.

q.s: In macroeconomic policy, the term 'fiscal dominance' refers to:
o: The Finance Commission's control over tax devolution
The RBI's control over the Government's borrowing programme
The dominance of direct taxes in Government revenue
Heavy Government borrowing that presses on money supply and inflation
q.x: Under fiscal dominance, large deficits constrain monetary policy; the fiscal deficit is a part of fiscal policy.

q.s: Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) in India are companies incorporated under the:
q.x: NBFCs are companies under the Companies Act and register with the RBI; they have no access to the RBI's Liquidity Adjustment Facility.

q.s: 100% FDI under the automatic route is allowed in NBFCs, but FDI is NOT permitted in:
q.x: FDI is prohibited in Nidhi companies.

q.s: The revenue from the Integrated GST (IGST) on an inter-State supply is finally settled to the:
q.x: GST is destination-based, so the State share of IGST goes to the consuming State; the Centre collects IGST.

q.s: Which component of GST is levied on inter-State supplies of goods and services?
q.x: IGST applies to inter-State supplies; UTGST applies to intra-UT supplies in UTs without a legislature.

q.s: In 2001, the time of presenting the Union Budget was moved from 5 pm to 11 am by Finance Minister:
q.x: Yashwant Sinha changed the Budget time in 2001.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Union Budget is correct?
o: The 1973-74 Budget is known as the 'Dream Budget'.
The 1997-98 Budget is known as the 'Black Budget'.
The first paperless (digital) Union Budget was presented in 2021.
The Budget time was moved to 11 am in 1991.
q.x: 1973-74 was the 'Black Budget' and 1997-98 the 'Dream Budget'; the time was changed in 2001.

q.s: Which is the largest source of net irrigated area in India (2021-22)?
q.x: Tubewells irrigate about 47.3% of the net irrigated area, canals about 24.7% and tanks only about 2.8%.

q.s: Which of the following statements about irrigation in India (2021-22) is correct?
o: The net irrigated area exceeds the gross irrigated area.
Canals are the second-largest source of net irrigated area.
Tanks are the second-largest source of net irrigated area.
Tanks irrigate about 12% of the net irrigated area.
q.x: Canals come second (24.7%); net irrigated area was 77.9 Mha and gross 120.3 Mha.

q.s: Which of the following kharif crops has the highest Minimum Support Price for 2026-27?
q.x: Sesamum has the highest kharif MSP (Rs 10,346 per quintal); sunflower got the largest hike.

q.s: The Minimum Support Price of wheat for Rabi Marketing Season 2026-27 is (Rs per quintal):
q.x: Wheat MSP for RMS 2026-27 is Rs 2,585; Rs 2,441 is the kharif 2026-27 MSP of common paddy.

q.s: The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 received the assent of the President on:
q.x: Assent came on 1 March 2014; the appointed day of bifurcation was 2 June 2014.

q.s: Andhra State, formed on 1 October 1953, had its capital at:
q.x: Andhra State (1953) had Kurnool as capital; Andhra Pradesh was formed on 1 November 1956 with Hyderabad as capital.

q.s: Potti Sriramulu died after a fast unto death for a separate Andhra State in:
q.x: Sriramulu died on 15 December 1952, after which Andhra State was announced.

q.s: The Rayalaseema plateau of Andhra Pradesh is made up mainly of:
q.x: The Rayalaseema plateau is Archaean gneiss with red soils; the coastal plains are alluvial.

q.s: Which of the following dam–river pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Krishna Raja Sagara (KRS) is on the Kaveri despite its name.

q.s: Monazite, found in the heavy-mineral beach sands of the Andhra coast, is an important source of:
q.x: Monazite is the source of thorium; the beach sands run from Srikakulam (Bhavanapadu) to Nellore.

q.s: Which of the following districts of Andhra Pradesh does NOT have heavy-mineral beach sand deposits?
q.x: Kurnool is inland; the beach sands extend along the coast from Srikakulam to Nellore.

q.s: Punganur, a native breed of Andhra Pradesh known for its very small size, is a breed of:
q.x: Punganur (Chittoor) is a dwarf cattle breed.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a native livestock breed of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Gir is a cattle breed of Gujarat; Punganur and Ongole are AP cattle breeds and Aseel an AP poultry breed.

q.s: The Meerut–Saharanpur–Muzaffarnagar sugar belt lies in:
q.x: The belt is in western Uttar Pradesh, which has the largest long-run share of India's sugar output.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a cooperative sugar centre of Maharashtra?
q.x: Gorakhpur is a sugar centre of Uttar Pradesh; Nasik, Pune, Satara, Sangli, Kolhapur and Sholapur are Maharashtra's cooperative centres.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the BIMARU States?
q.x: BIMARU stands for Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh.

q.s: Araku coffee, grown by tribal farmers of Andhra Pradesh, is cultivated mainly in the area of which ITDA?
q.x: Araku coffee is grown in the Paderu ITDA area over about one lakh acres.

q.s: The Girijan Cooperative Corporation (GCC), which buys minor forest produce from tribals and runs PDS depots in Andhra Pradesh, is a:
o: Statutory body under the Forest Rights Act
q.x: GCC is a State cooperative set up in 1956, not a Central PSU.

q.s: Under Section 2(c) of the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992, minorities are notified by the:
o: President on the advice of Parliament
q.x: The Centre notifies minorities under Section 2(c).

q.s: Which State has had a Uniform Civil Code in force since January 2025?
q.x: Uttarakhand's Uniform Civil Code came into force in January 2025.

q.s: The upwelling off the Peru–Chile coast, linked to the Humboldt current, supports a huge fishery of:
q.x: The Humboldt upwelling supports anchoveta; the Kerala upwelling supports oil sardine and mackerel.

q.s: The coastal upwelling off Namibia is associated with the:
q.x: The cold Benguela current drives upwelling off Namibia.

q.s: The DST scheme PURSE gives grants to universities on the basis of:
q.x: PURSE rewards research-publication performance; FIST upgrades laboratories.

q.s: Which DST scheme supports the upgrading of laboratories and infrastructure in university departments?
q.x: FIST upgrades departmental S&T infrastructure; SATHI provides shared infrastructure and SAIF regional access to instruments.

q.s: Matsya 6000, the crewed submersible of India's Deep Ocean Mission, is being built by:
q.x: The National Institute of Ocean Technology, Chennai builds Matsya 6000, designed to take three people to 6,000 m.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Deep Ocean Mission is correct?
o: Matsya 6000 is designed to take five people to 6,000 m.
Its nodal ministry is the Ministry of Earth Sciences.
Its nodal ministry is the Ministry of Science and Technology.
q.x: The Ministry of Earth Sciences runs the mission, approved in June 2021 with Rs 4,077 crore for five years.

q.s: The 100th launch from Sriharikota, in January 2025, was:
q.x: GSLV-F15 carrying NVS-02 was the 100th launch from SHAR; PSLV-C21 (2012) was ISRO's 100th space mission.

q.s: The Third Launch Pad being built at Sriharikota is meant mainly for the:
q.x: The First Launch Pad serves PSLV and SSLV; the Third Launch Pad is for the NGLV.

q.s: India is NOT a member of which of the following export-control regimes?

Is the largest gland of the body

The cheetah was declared extinct in India before Independence.
